doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Electric bands as Miles's Gil Evans color
summary: Kirchner suggests Miles's electric bands recreated Gil Evans's orchestral color, and Liebman agrees that color serves the story like harmony.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: I have a feeling, and I’m not alone in thinking this, that his electric bands were his way of reproducing the stuff he did with Gil Evans, but in an electric setting, but with him as the centerpiece.
That’s a valid – I could see that.
But trying to do with electric instruments . . .

Color, and the storytelling aspect of what color does. What color does is it enhances the story. It’s what harmony does. Harmony enhances the melody. We have – 99% of the music in the world doesn’t have harmony in it. It’s been doing fine for 5,000 years. But when you have harmony – which, thank you, Western world – you deepen the emotional impact of the melody. You broaden it. You change the color of it. Gil: master of color, at that period, for sure. I never thought of it like that, but you have a valid point. I could understand that.
